scores.evidence: our PCI DSS scope stays at SAQ A (reduced, not zero)
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (RLS via per-transaction tenant context, transactional outbox/inbox, PSP idempotency keys derived from attempt IDs, at-least-once signed webhooks, gapless numbering at finalization) are described accurately, including the real limits of each guarantee.

scores.evidence: each tenant (a SaaS company) uses it to bill its own end customers for subscriptions and usage
scores.rationale: The platform-vs-module ambiguity is resolved explicitly and core billing capabilities are phased credibly, but trials, dunning specifics and end-customer entitlement continuity are thin or only deferred.

scores.evidence: Strong (serializable or row-locked transactions on one primary) for ledger, invoice finalization and payment attempts
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, data ownership and consistency choices are stated once and honored everywhere (RLS from Phase 0, outbox/inbox on every async path, adapters for all vendors), with no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: 0 duplicates and 0 amount mismatches across ≥ 10k fault scenarios; 0 unexplained reconciliation breaks over 2 cycles
scores.rationale: V0–V8 tie each check to a specific risk with measurable thresholds labeled as assumptions, run the riskiest checks before commitment (V1 before dependents, V4/V5 before live charges), and continue in production via reconciliation and SLOs.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: needs tenant count, end customers, invoices/month and peak usage events/s at 12 months
scores.rationale: Assumptions (a)–(c) and every budget are explicitly labeled ASSUMPTION or UNKNOWN with a named supplier and confirmation path, and each decision row states what changes if the assumption fails.

scores.evidence: crashes between the PSP call and commit
scores.rationale: Covers the hardest domain failures — duplicate charges, out-of-order webhooks, lost usage events, ledger imbalance, cross-tenant leaks — each with concrete detection (reconciliation, balance monitor, dedup) and containment (kill switches, DLQ, shadow mode).

scores.evidence: Rollback is redeploying the previous image. Migrations only add things.
scores.rationale: Deployment, rehearsed rollback, expand-then-contract migrations, domain-meaningful alerts (outbox lag, reconciliation breaks, invoice-run dashboard), on-call, DR drills and an explicit operational-complexity budget sized to a 5–8 person team.

scores.evidence: Unit-cost dashboard against the target take rate
scores.rationale: Cost drivers are named (PSP platform fees, tax-engine calls, infra), unit cost is measured from Phase 3 and gated at GA, but cost scaling with usage and the build-cost side of the build-vs-buy trade are not quantified.

Every decision is classified R2/R3 with revisit triggers, irreversible points (first live charge, legacy decommissioning) are gated by validations, and exit paths (silo cells, Adyen via the same adapter, TigerBeetle, Kinesis flip) are explicit.

scores.evidence: Modular monolith (billing core) plus a separate usage-ingest service
scores.rationale: Starts with two deployables, Postgres-backed queue and managed services, defers Temporal, streaming stores, multi-region and cells behind named triggers, with no component lacking a stated need.

scores.evidence: Killing the worker between commit and outbox dispatch produces neither a lost nor a duplicated event.
scores.rationale: Phases have dependency-justified order, a concrete first slice, checkable exit criteria, specific technology decisions, and every validation row states what happens if it fails.

checklist.evidence: Money is `bigint` minor units plus ISO 4217 currency.
A finalized invoice never changes; corrections go through credit notes
Payment attempts whose PSP idempotency key is derived from `payment_attempt_id`
Payment-method capture through PSP-hosted fields only
Postgres Row-Level Security reads `app.tenant_id`, which is set per transaction from the authenticated context
Dedup on (`tenant_id`, `event_id`). Late-event policy: events accepted until invoice finalization, then credited to the next period
Subscription lifecycle: create, upgrade or downgrade with proration, pause, cancel
Buy tax: Stripe Tax or Avalara behind a `TaxEngine` adapter
Daily reconciliation: every PSP balance transaction ↔ a ledger entry
Prepaid credits, wallets, entitlements service, quotes/CPQ: pull forward when design partners need them
Build the billing core (it is the product). Buy the PSP: Stripe Connect behind a `PaymentProvider` adapter

traps.evidence: Money is `bigint` minor units plus ISO 4217 currency
Append-only double-entry ledger is the system of record for balances
Inbound PSP webhooks go through an inbox dedup table
Card data never touches our systems (PSP-hosted fields)

note: An exceptionally rigorous, technically precise plan that avoids all five traps and gates every irreversible step; the few gaps are trials/time-zone detail, dunning specifics, end-customer entitlement continuity, and cost-scaling quantification.
